questions.scenario: A student in your class drops their lunch and has nothing to eat. What is your first reaction?

options.text: I quickly collect some money/food from everyone to make a new lunch for them.
I help them pick up the fallen food and put it in the compost/dustbin.
I get angry at the kid who accidentally bumped into them and demand an apology.
I silently share my own tiffin with them so they don't feel embarrassed.
I sit with them, share some of my food, and help them study for the next class to cheer them up.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You have a completely free Sunday. Which of these activities sounds like a good time?

options.text: Setting up a stall to sell cookies and raise funds for a charity.
Going with a group to clean up a dirty local park or beach.
Participating in a debate competition about equality and justice.
Visiting an old age home to play games with the elderly.
Going to a local community center or slum to teach free math and science classes to kids.
None of these.

questions.scenario: What kind of real-life story or documentary makes you the most emotional?

options.text: A story about a man who built a massive kitchen that feeds 100,000 poor people daily.
A story about saving polar bears and the melting ice caps.
A story of a brave lawyer who fought to free an innocent person from jail.
A story of a kind woman who personally treats and hugs sick street kids.
A story about a young girl who fought against all odds to build a school for girls in her village.
None of these.

questions.scenario: There is a stray dog in your society. What do you do?

options.text: Start a WhatsApp group to collect funds to build a small shelter for it.
Plant some trees or make a shaded mud-bed so it can stay cool in the summer.
Fight with the society uncle who is trying to throw stones at the dog.
Bring milk and biscuits from my house and feed it with my own hands.
Create posters and educate the kids in the society on how to safely treat and care for animals.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you could have a 'Social Superpower', what would you choose?

options.text: The power to magically generate infinite food and money for the poor.
The power to instantly heal polluted rivers and grow dead trees.
The power to force everyone in the world to speak the truth and be fair.
The power to take away someone's physical or mental pain just by hugging them.
The power to instantly transfer all the knowledge in the world into a child's mind.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Your school is organizing a grand fest. What responsibility do you take?

options.text: Managing the charity stall and keeping track of all the donations.
Making strict rules that no plastic cups or plates will be used in the fest.
Making sure even the shy or weak students get a fair chance to perform on stage.
Staying back after the fest is over to help the cleaning staff and sweepers.
Setting up an awareness booth to educate students about mental health or rural literacy.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Every noble work has a boring or tough part. What can you tolerate happily?

options.text: Doing boring math to calculate budgets and expenses for a charity event.
Picking up dirty, smelly garbage with my hands to clean a park.
Reading hundreds of pages of boring law books to win an argument.
Sitting quietly for hours just listening to a very sad person crying.
Repeating the same basic math lesson 50 times patiently until a slow-learning kid understands.
None of these.

questions.scenario: What triggers your anger the most when you step out of your house?

options.text: Seeing perfectly good food or clothes being thrown away in the garbage.
Seeing someone comfortably throw a plastic wrapper out of a moving car.
Seeing a strong person or a senior bullying a helpless junior.
Seeing an old person struggling to cross the road while everyone ignores them.
Seeing a young child working at a tea stall instead of being in school with books.
None of these.

questions.scenario: What kind of posts do you usually share or like on your social media?

options.text: Crowd-funding links to help someone pay their heavy hospital bills.
Posts about saving water, planting trees, and global warming facts.
Strong posts about feminism, equality, or fighting against discrimination.
Sending long, personal, sweet messages to friends who are feeling low.
Sharing free study resources, educational videos, and scholarships for students in need.
None of these.

questions.scenario: In your friend group, what title fits you the best?

options.text: The Organizer (Gets everyone together to do something productive).
The Nature Lover (Prefers animals and mountains over crowded cafes).
The Rebel/Fighter (Always ready to debate for what is right).
The 'Mom/Dad' of the group (Takes care of everyone and listens to their problems).
The Mentor (Always teaching something new, giving advice, or helping with studies).
None of these.
